text:
olivia_support: FYI — AcmeCo on Dedicated pool d-nyc-3 is getting repeated 429s and large tail latencies. They sent a repro with very long-context requests (~120k tokens) and saw KV cache thrashing. Attaching logs from their request stream.
jamal_oncall: Can you paste the first 429 and related runtime logs here? Need node IDs + GPU host.
olivia_support: Pasting condensed log snippet: 
```
[2026-01-12T14:22:03Z] tenant=acmeco pool=d-nyc-3 node=gpu-17 request_id=rr-9ab kv_cache_miss=0.87 eviction_count=12438 throttle=1 error=429
[2026-01-12T14:22:04Z] tenant=acmeco tail_latency=1450ms seq_len=120384 kv_fragmentation=0.73
```
jamal_oncall: Thanks. That's classic KV pressure signals — eviction count + fragmentation high. I'm going to check node metrics.
irene_sre: Ran quick probe on gpu-17: memory free is low, kv cache usage ~96% of assigned GPU shard. Eviction spikes match the timestamps. No OOM but heavy compaction activity.
deploy-bot: autoscaler: attempted scale up from 6 -> 9 nodes at 14:22:05Z, quota hit in region:yes, scale prevented.
raman_eng: Noting that autoscaler failing to acquire extra nodes will leave long-context workloads to compete for KV cache. Possible noisy neighbor — which tenants were active concurrently?
olivia_support: AcmeCo reported two heavy sessions and another internal tenant "sim-bench" running many parallel long-context tests at the same time.
jamal_oncall: Repro steps I tried locally: spawn two sessions with repeated context extension to 100k+, observe eviction rate ramp and 429s within ~200k tokens across both sessions.
irene_sre: Quick dump from kv inspector (condensed):
```
node=gpu-17 kv_total_entries=14,240,312 avg_entry=520B active_ratio=0.92 fragmentation_bytes=1.3GB eviction_queue_len=3600
```
raman_eng: Hmm — fragmentation_bytes that high indicates allocation churn and inability to coalesce during compaction. There's a known allocator path that regresses on long-lived KV entries. Might be causing slow eviction throughput.
jamal_oncall: Workarounds to try now for AcmeCo: 1) ask them to trim context or switch to rolling windowing, 2) temporarily reduce per-tenant kv_max_entries, 3) enable prefix caching if their workload is prefix-heavy, 4) bump to a dedicated burst node (if quota allows).
olivia_support: Customer prefers a config change vs app-side changes. Can we reduce kv_max_entries for them from 16M -> 8M to steal headroom?
irene_sre: We can patch their tenant config to lower entries; this will cause more eviction but free contiguous segments faster. Applying change now to tenant acmeco on gpu-17.
deploy-bot: config-change: tenant=acmeco kv_max_entries=8000000 applied by irene_sre at 14:38:12Z
raman_eng: Also opened a runtime issue (PR #2345) to improve compaction; reference: runtime/kv/compact-fix. This will take an engineering rollout. For short term, lowering kv_max_entries + enabling prefix cache should mitigate.
jamal_oncall: After config change, monitoring shows eviction_count fell 35% and fragmentation down to ~0.44. Throttles dropped but not gone — tail latency still elevated for a few requests while cache warms.
olivia_support: I notified AcmeCo about temporary config and suggested app-side windowing. They accepted the change; no billing impact expected.
raman_eng: Long-term follow-ups: 1) runtime patch in PR #2345 (needs perf sign-off), 2) autoscaler should surface quota failures more loudly and offer fallback policy (route to burst pool), 3) add per-node fragmentation alert at 0.5+ to catch earlier.
irene_sre: Created ticket INC-4591 to track mitigation and scheduled a postmortem if we see repeat in 72h.
ojamal_oncall: (minor) we should add a small playbook snippet to runbook: how to safely reduce kv_max_entries per-tenant and expected cache-warm timeline.
olivia_support: I'll draft the mail to AcmeCo and update the support ticket with steps we took + link INC-4591. Closing slack thread unless new regressions show up. :white_check_mark:
